sentences.text: Shri M.K. Gavne - Advocate for the appellant.

Smt. Shanti Tiwari - Panel Lawyer for the respondent-S
Record of the Court below is received.
Heard on the question of admission.
Admit.
Also heard on I.A. No.30588/2023, which is first application filed on behalf of appellant suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

Appellant has been convicted by the trial Court under Sections 376(1) and 506 Part II of the IPC and sentenced him to undergo R.I. for 1 year and R.I. for 6 months with fine of Rs.10000/- and Rs.5000/- with default stipulations.

The counsel for appellant submits that the trial Court has not properly appreciated the oral and documentary evidence available on record and committed error in convicting appellant for the aforesaid offence.

It is contended by the counsel that the prosecution story even if taken into consideration on its face value, there is no iota of doubt that the present appellant as well as prosecutrix were having affair and they were in touch personally as well as through mobile phone on more than 400 occasions and the said fact is also not disputed, even appreciated by the trial Court in paragraph 10 of the judgment.

It is further contended by the counsel that the paragraph 10 of the judgment makes it abundantly clear that the present appellant deserves to be enlarged on bail taking into consideration the fact that age of the prosecutrix at the time of commission of offence was 36 years and the factum of affair as well as contact through mobile phone on multiple occasions has not been disputed by the prosecutrix.
It is also contended by the counsel that the DNA report is negative and even the brother of the prosecutrix turned hostile.
This appeal is of the year 2023 and there is no possibility of final hearing of this appeal in near future, therefore, the jail sentence of appellant be suspended and he be released on bail.

sentences.text: It is contended by the counsel that on the false pretext of marriage, the prosecutrix was pitchforked to enter into physical relationship and thereby the appellant committed the offence under the provisions of Section 376 of IPC.
Thus, taking into consideration the direct allegations which have been duly proved by the prosecution beyond reasonable doubt, therefore, the appellant is not entitled to be released on bail.
Heard the submissions advanced on behalf of the parties and perused the record.

A perusal of records it reflect that the prosecutrix has not disputed the aspect that she was having affair with the present appellant and they had in touch through mobile phone on more than 400 occasions.
It is also undisputed that the prosecutrix was aged about 36 years at the time of commission of said offence.

Considering the aforesaid totality of the circumstances of the case including the factum of consent as well as the age of the prosecutrix and also the age of the present appellant, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is inclined to consider and allow the application.
Accordingly, I.A. No.30588/2023 is allowed.

It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned, the custodial sentence of appellant shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail for securing his presence before the trial Court concerned on 24.07.2024 and on such other dates as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
List this case for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.
(MANINDER S. BHATTI) JUDGE sp Anup Dube vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141296526/
